questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
options: "I have lived here for 5 years."
"I have lived there in 2019."
"I lived here since 2019."
"I am living here since five years."
questions.explanation: Present perfect connects past to present ("for 5 years"); a finished time like "in 2019" requires past simple.

questions.question: Which signal words typically indicate the past simple, not the present perfect?
options: "yesterday", "last week", "ago"
"yet", "ever", "since"
"always", "never", "just"
"for", "so far", "already"
questions.explanation: "Yesterday", "last week" and "ago" pin the action to finished past time, requiring past simple.

questions.question: Which conditional describes an unreal or hypothetical present situation?
options: Second conditional — "If I won the lottery, I would travel"
Zero conditional — "If you heat ice, it melts"
First conditional — "If it rains, I will stay home"
Third conditional — "If I had studied, I would have passed"
questions.explanation: The second conditional (If + past, would + infinitive) expresses hypothetical present or future situations.

questions.question: What is the passive voice version of "The committee approved the plan"?
options: "The plan was approved by the committee."
"The plan approved the committee."
"The committee was approved by the plan."
"The plan is approving the committee."
questions.explanation: In the passive, the object becomes the subject: "The plan was approved (by the committee)."

questions.question: Which conditional pattern expresses a real future possibility?
options: First conditional: If + present, will + infinitive
Zero conditional: If + present, present
Second conditional: If + past, would + infinitive
Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + participle
questions.explanation: The first conditional ("If it rains, I will stay home") describes realistic future possibilities.
